# Set-up

`CellBender` performs a lot better when provided with the input parameters `expected-cells` and `total-droplets-included`. We can estimate both of these input parameters from the resulting knee plot. 

Please note also that there are multiple issues open on `CellBender` github suggesting that it may struggle on multiplexed data as its designed to be run on a per-sample basis. [issue1](https://github.com/broadinstitute/CellBender/issues/421), [issue2](https://github.com/broadinstitute/CellBender/issues/373).

In addition, while not officially documented in their documentations, the authors do not recommend running it on the HTO features [issue3](https://github.com/broadinstitute/CellBender/issues/223)



# Make Kneeplot

Let's make a kneeplot and highlight potential thresholds for `-total-droplet-included`. The `-total-droplet-included` does not have to be exact- every droplet/barcode past that threshold will however be treated as an empty droplet. 

Make a function. This will show the first knee and inflection point (for cell calls), and second knee and inflection point (for ambient).

```{r}
run_kneeplot <- function(counts, 
                         label_df, 
                         name){
  bcrank <- barcodeRanks(counts) #using DropletUtils function
  bcrank_filtered <- bcrank[!duplicated(bcrank$rank), ]# only show unique points for plotting speed
  
  #re-run compute ranks with bounds
  #higher bound based on previous inflection point, lower at 0
  bounds_for_ambient <- c(0,
                        bcrank@metadata$inflection)
  
  bcrank_ambient <- barcodeRanks(counts_raw, 
                               fit.bounds=bounds_for_ambient) 
  
  y_lines <- data.frame(name=c("knee","inflection", "knee_ambient"),
                                         num=c(bcrank@metadata$knee,
                                               bcrank@metadata$inflection,
                                               bcrank_ambient@metadata$knee))
  
  plot <- ggplot(data = bcrank_filtered, aes(x = log10(rank), log10(total))) + geom_point()+
    geom_vline(data= label_df, mapping = aes(xintercept = log10(num), colour = name)) +
    geom_hline(data= y_lines, mapping = aes(yintercept = log10(num), colour = name)) +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = unname(Polychrome::alphabet.colors(nrow(label_df) + nrow(y_lines))))+
    theme_bw() + theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.text = element_text(size=15), 
                       legend.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "cm"), legend.key.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "cm"))+
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 2)))+
    ggtitle(sprintf('Knee plot:\n%s', name))
  
  
  return(list(plot=plot,metric=y_lines))
  
}

```

So from the exported metadata, we can get an estimate for the number of cells we're expecting. 

```{r}
meta_raw$type %>% table()
```

In this case, we can sum up doublet, multiplet and singlet. 

```{r}
meta_raw$type[meta_raw$type %in% c("doublet", "singlet", "multiplet")] %>% length()
```

So that's approximately 19k cells. 


```{r, fig.align='center', fig.height=4, fig.width=6}

#set same test thresholds for all
label_df <- data.frame(name=c("cells_19k", "droplet_40k"),
                       num = c(19000, 40000))

out <- run_kneeplot(count = counts_raw, label_df = label_df, name="Lung Cancer Dataset")


out$plot
```

```{r}
DT::datatable(out$metric)
```
